meta.title: How Checkout is built
meta.dek: Ten components in four groups take an order from the web app to the warehouse. Click a part for what it does, a pin for a decision, or step through the flows.
meta.description: An interactive architecture walkthrough of an invented checkout system, around a technical architecture diagram.

theme.concept: A plain engineering page: ink on white paper, one accent for what moves.

chapters.title: The parts and the paths between them

blocks.alt: Checkout's architecture: a web app and API gateway, an order service with its database, payments with a card processor and a planned fraud check, and an event bus feeding email and warehouse workers.

orders.title: Order service
orders.text: Saves each order in the orders database, asks Payments to charge the card, then publishes order.placed.

payments.title: Payments
payments.text: Charges the card through the processor and retries a timeout twice before failing the order.

bus.title: Event bus
bus.text: Carries order.placed to the workers, so a slow email never holds up a purchase.

cards.title: Card processor
cards.text: An outside vendor. Its outages show up here first.

pins.title: Decision: retry twice, then fail
pins.text: A third retry doubled checkout latency in the load test; two keep p95 under a second.

pins.title: Question: one bus or two?
pins.text: Warehouse sync may move to its own bus when order volume triples.

blocks.text: The fraud check is planned for next quarter; it joins the payment path between Payments and the card processor.
